label: doc_title
text: LOCAL AND GENERAL NEWS.

label: text
text: Lighting-up time to-day is at 6 p.m.

label: text
text: A German missionary has been murdered near Omsk in Siberia by Eathonlan Communists according to a report to the Gustaf Adolf Society.

label: text
text: Mr. F. H. Loseby, a new solicitor, was admitted to practice yesterday by the Chief Justice, on the application of the Attorney General. Mr. Loseby is joining Messrs. Lee and Russell.

label: text
text: A new feature in local aquaties—the swimming race' across the harbour—is to be introduced by the Army sports authorities tomorrow, the course being from the Kowloon wharf to the R.A.S.C. camber.

label: text
text: Nos. 14e., d., and e., Robinson road were sold yesterday at Measrs, Lammer's Auction Rooms, the price in each case being $1,200; a rise of $200 on opening price. Mr. Fung Woin bought Nos. e. and e. and Mr. Man Foo No. d.

label: text
text: Berlin, September 30. The Governor of the Italian colony Erythren on the Red Sea has concluded a treaty with the Innam of Yemen giving Italy important accessions in return for economic aid and the supply of certain materials.

label: text
text: The Hong Kong & Canton Ice Manufacturing Co., Ltd. is to hold the 5th annual meeting (at the town office, No. 2, Lower Albert Road), at 12 noon on November 2. The transfer books will be closed from to-day to November 2, inclusive.

label: text
text: A report from the “China Mail” correspondent at Pakkal (received by mail) confirms the Naval intelligence that all strike pickets at the port of Kongmoon withdrew on October 10. The merchants there were looking forward to the trip, from Hong Kong, of the s.s. “San Nam Hoi.”

label: text
text: Soerabayna, Dutch Indies, October 5.—Five Europeans and six natives were killed here to-day, in a bomb explosion. The bomb was hurled at a government official as he was riding in a procession given in honour of a national holiday. The bomb fell short and the official was not injured but the explosion came in the centre of a crowd of persons densely packed together watching the parade. label: text
text: Rico prices in Shanghai on October 9 were unchanged from recent high levels, being quoted at $17.40 to $19 per pcll, the latter price being the maximum under the official price restrictions recently introduced.

label: text
text: A new tax came into force at Taingtao on October 5, namely, a minimum charge of $50 on all motor cars landed at Taingtao. Summer visitors will not be so ready to take cars from Shanghai for a couple of months stay if they are taxed to this extent.

label: text
text: Peking, Oct. 10.—In view of the fact that almost all the Branch offices of the Russo-Asiatic Bank in China are located in foreign concessions, the Waichłopu, fearing that books and documents of the Bank might be lost or destroyed yesterday asked the Diplomatic Corps up keep watch over those branches.—Toho

label: text
text: It is said that the cost of repairs at Port Arthur to the Chinese warship Hajichi will amount to $120,000 and that she will be completed on October 24, and that then the warships "Haichen" and "Chungho" will also proceed there for repair, the cost of repair to the former, being estimated at $20,000, and the later $80,000.

label: text
text: The Sin Min Yi Pao, an official organ of the Chinese Association for Mass Education in Peking reappeared on the National Anniversary day, (October 10). The editor-in-chief is Mr. Chang Yuosen. This paper has been suspended more than a year. It adopts the simple style vernacular language in its columns, as the Association for Mass Education desired to employ the thousand characters, which are taught in mass education schools, in the newspaper to spread its mass education programme.

label: text
text: A Cantonese, victory in China was predicted by Ambassador L. M. Karakhan when interviewed in Vladivostok. China will eventually be free from both the militaries and from unequal foreign treaties, M. Karakhan declared, indicating that "the present period of internal militaristic domination and external oppression by foreign Powers must be considered only as a transient phase." M. Karakhan said that the treaty between Soviet Russia and China had set an example of an equal treaty, along the lines of which future foreign treaties with China must follow.

label: doc_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL

label: text
text: Mr. and Mrs. A. R. Sutherland are returning to the Colony in the early part of December.

label: text
text: Mrs. Frederick's, of Glenealy Hotel, left for Shanghai and Japan to-day on a short holiday.

label: text
text: Harbin, Oct. 9.—Mr. Cheruniff, who recently was appointed as Soviet Acting Ambassador to Peking, arrived here this morning en route to his new post.

label: text
text: Deserving much better patronage than was "extended," Lucia di Lammermoor" was presented by the Royal Italian Opera Company (under Sig. A. Carpi) at the "Star" Theatre last night. To-night's farewell performance will be "Aida" which is very favourably spoken of.

label: text
text: Mr. P. P. J. Wodehouse, Deputy Superintendent of Police, who has been on. "Home" leave for some months past, is due to return to Hong Kong by the P. & O. s.s. "Malwa," which sails from London on November 12. Also a passenger on the same steamer is Mrs. A. O. Lang.

label: text
text: Miss Mable McNeill, of "Minneapolis," "Minnesota," has arrived in Shanghai for a visit of several months' duration to "her brother-in-law and sister, Mr. and Mrs. Arthur P. Henningsen."

label: text
text: The forthcoming wedding is announced of John Francis Shirley, Chief Electrical Artifier, of the H.M.S. "Hermes," to Certrude Ellen Davis, of The Mount, the Peak; Carl Peder Nissen, merchant of Shameen, to Arla Kristiane Petroniella Poulsen (nee Jensen), widow, of Copenhagen.

label: text
text: After 25 years of continuous service in the Chinese Customs, Mr. C. W. Cunningham left Shanghai on the 12th instant, on well earned Home leave, accompanied by his eldest son and daughter, and expects to be absent for seven months, Mr. Cunningham, who has been in charge of the Dynamite Magazine for over 19 years, will visit the explosives factories of Messrs. Nobel and Co., Ltd., and dear, Scotland, with the object of securing a more up-to-date technical and practical knowledge of high explosives.

label: text
text: .Moscow, September 22.—The Electrotechnical Trust has decided to introduce “Fordisation” of production. It means highest specialisation and division of labour and quicker process of production. It is expected that all factories of the Electrotechnical Trust will yield goods for 35 million roubles as against 27 million roubles during last year.

label: text
text: Miss Mattie Mögabgab, who has been in Kuling for the past month, returned to Shanghai on October 9.

label: text
text: Something new in Chinese barber shop announcements. The following notice is displayed at a barber shop in Avenue Edward VII. Shanghai: "Hairdressing 50 cents: Face shaving 40 cents: Lady dressinging 60 cents." No rush has been reported for the last item.

label: text
text: -The King's Own Scottish Borders arrived on Friday by the "Neura" and as the East Surreys will not be leaving till the following Wednesday a few sports event between the two Regiments have been arranged. A football match is fixed for Saturday and a boxing tournament on Monday evening.

label: text
text: Thirty-seven Chinese military officers belonging to Marshal Chang Tao-lin's army, headed by Colonel Lo Yun-kuei, a staff officer and concurrently Chief Military Instructor, arrived in Tokyo on October 8 in order to enter various military colleges in Japan.

label: text
text: A public telephone service has been introduced at Kungyick (in the Sunning district), the exchange at Kongmoon being connected to the Sunning Railway wires. For each message to or from Kungyick a charge of 30 cents is made.—Our own correspondent.

label: text
text: Nine recruiting offices opened by General Sun Chuan-fang, in Shanghai, were closed on October 8. The offices were opened at the shops, hotels, and in huts on vacant ground and resulted in getting about 100 recruits daily since October 1, when they were first opened. Seventy recruits obtained in Nantao were sent to Nanking on October 8. Another 40 obtained in Chapel were also despatched northward. One hundred men from Taichow, in Chekiang, passed through Shanghai to Nanking, while a small party of men who received training in Nanking returned to Shanghai on October 8 and were sent to Woosung Fort's.

label: text
text: Mrs. Frank P. Lockhart, wife of the American Consul-General at Hankow, left Shanghai for Hankow on October 8 accompanied by her son and daughter.

label: text
text: Mr. P. P. J. Wodehouse, C.I.E., Deputy Superintendent of Police, is due back from furlough shortly. He is travelling by the s.a. "Malwa" which leaves London on November 12.

label: text
text: A marriage has been arranged, and will take place in Colombo, in February, 1927, between Arthur, only son of Mr. and Mrs. F. L. Clark, of Lancing, Sussex, England, and Maev, younger daughter of the late Rev. H. McVittie Taylor, of Dublin, and of Mrs. Patrick Mullane.

label: text
text: Governor-General Leonard Wood returned to Malacunan Palace from Sternberg Hospital on the 14th instant. He has been in the hospital for several weeks after undergoing a serious operation. The operation was completely successful, and the Governor-General's health improved rapidly.

label: text
text: Mr. Allan Cameron, Orient Manager for the Canadian Pacific Railway Company and the Canadian Pacific Steamships Company, will return to Hong Kong by the R.M.S. "Empress of Canada." Mr. Cameron has been away from Hong Kong for the past few months on a business trip to the head office of the Company in Canada. During his absence Mr. P. A. Cox, assistant, Oriental Manager, Shanghai has been in charge and he will now be returning to Shanghai.

label: text
text: Worl has been received in Manila of the death on September 5 of John Rex Thompson of Seattle, well known in Manila as a shriner who has made three pilgrimages to the Orient with Nile Temple. As in Mason, Mr. Thompson held practically every office in Nile Temple. He was its director for seven years and besides the three pilgrimages to the Orient he made 12 to Alasya. He was known through out the Northwest for his hearty good cheer and fellowship.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEWS.

label: text
text: Mr. F. H. Holdman, of the local Post Office, is returning after furlough together with Mrs. Holdman early next month. They left London on the s.s. "Delta". on October 7.

label: text
text: Mrs. E. B. Gregory, the wife of Mr. Gregory of the British Cigarette Company, is expected to return to Shanghai on October 23 from a visit to her home in America.

label: text
text: The engagement is announced between Herbert John Weston Peck, eldest son of the late Captain Herbert W. Peck, Sarawak Service, and Joan Tasker Evans, second daughter of the late Mr. and Mrs. Evans, of Fair Elms, Pinner.

label: text
text: Mr. W. Willshire, for many years associated with the Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels, Ltd., and until recently manager of the Palace Hotel, Shanghai, is a through passenger to Bombay, where he is to take over the management of an important group of hotels.

label: text
text: To-morrow H.E. the Governor and Lady Clementi will be At Home at Government House to a representative gathering of the East Surrey Regiment when it is anticipated that nearly 300 will be present (including the wives and families of N.C.O.'s and men). They will be entertained to tea and there will also be dancing, Lady Clementi having arranged for lady partners. A play by local amateurs will be given in the grounds and musical items in the ball room.

label: text
text: Calcutta accorded a most cordial welcome to, India's distinguished visitors from overseas when they arrived at Howard on September 27. The South African Deputation was received on the platform by the Mayor and Corporation, the Sheriff of Calcutta, Mr. Lindsay representing the Government of Bengal. Sir Devaprasad Sarvadhikary, a member of the recent Government of India, and representatives of South Africa, and representatives of public bodies.
